regulations.context: Electrical resistance limits of antistatic materials
Pressurized enclosures for flammable mixture environments

tests.description: Marking on major part of ME EQUIPMENT for CATEGORY AP or APG parts, not repeated on detachable parts that can only be used with the marked equipment
ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTS contain indication enabling RESPONSIBLE ORGANIZATION to distinguish between CATEGORY AP and APG parts
Marking clearly indicates which parts are CATEGORY AP or APG when only certain ME EQUIPMENT parts are CATEGORY AP or APG
Common requirements for CATEGORY AP and CATEGORY APG ME EQUIPMENT
CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES between points of POWER SUPPLY CORD connection according to Table 12 for one MEANS OF PATIENT PROTECTION
Connections protected against accidental disconnection in NORMAL USE, or connection/disconnection only with a TOOL (excluding circuits in G.5.3 and G.6.3)
CATEGORY AP and APG not provided with a DETACHABLE POWER SUPPLY CORD, except when circuit complied with G.5.3 and G.6.3
Opening of ENCLOSURE providing protection against penetration of gases or vapours only possible with a TOOL

ENCLOSURE complies with requirements to minimize arcing and sparking due to penetration of foreign objects: no openings on top covers except for controls; side openings prevent penetration of 4mm diameter rod; base plate openings prevent penetration of 12mm diameter rod

Short circuiting conductor to conductive part without explosive gases, where insulation may contact FLAMMABLE AESTHETIC MIXTURE WITH OXYGEN or NITROUS OXIDE, ignitable gases, or oxygen, did not result in loss of integrity, unacceptable temperature, or HAZARDOUS SITUATION

Electrostatic charges prevented on CATEGORY AP and APG ME EQUIPMENT by combination of appropriate measures: use of antistatic materials, provision of electrically conductive paths to conductive floor, protective earth or potential equalization system
Electrical resistance limits of aesthetic tubing, mattresses and pads, castor tires, and other antistatic material complied with ISO 2882 based on measurements per ISO 1853, ISO 2878 and ISO 23529
Corona cannot be produced by components or parts operating at more than 2000 V a.c. or 2400 V d.c. not included in ENCLOSURES complying with G.5.4 or G.5.5
Requirements and tests for CATEGORY AP ME EQUIPMENT, parts and components

ME EQUIPMENT, its parts or components do not ignite FLAMMABLE AESTHETIC MIXTURES WITH AIR under NORMAL USE and CONDITIONS based on compliance with G.5.2 to G.5.5; alternatively complied with IEC 60079-0 for pressurized, sand-filled, or oil immersed enclosures

ME EQUIPMENT in contact with gas mixtures in NORMAL USE not producing sparks and not resulting in surface temperatures above 150°C (restricted airflow) or 200°C (unrestricted vertical air circulation) measured at 25°C
ME EQUIPMENT producing sparks in NORMAL USE complied with temperature requirements of G.5.2 and Umax and Imax occurring in their circuits

requirements.description: Marking on major part of ME EQUIPMENT for CATEGORY AP or APG, not repeated on detachable parts usable only with marked equipment
Accompanying documents must enable RESPONSIBLE ORGANIZATION to distinguish between CATEGORY AP and APG parts
Marking must clearly indicate which parts are CATEGORY AP or APG when only certain parts have that category
Creepage and clearances per Table 12; connections protected against accidental disconnection; no detachable power supply cord for CATEGORY AP/APG
Enclosure openings only accessible with tool; enclosure minimizes arcing/sparking; side openings <4mm rod; base openings <12mm rod
Electrostatic charges must be prevented; antistatic material resistance per ISO 2882
No corona from components operating above 2000V AC or 2400V DC outside compliant enclosures
ME EQUIPMENT must not ignite FLAMMABLE AESTHETIC MIXTURES WITH AIR in NORMAL USE
Surface temperature limits: 150°C restricted, 200°C unrestricted airflow at 25°C ambient, no spark generation
Spark-producing equipment must comply with G.5.2 temperature requirements and Umax/Imax circuit requirements

semantic_fragments.content: For CATEGORY AP and APG ME EQUIPMENT, electrostatic charges must be prevented by a combination of appropriate measures including: use of antistatic materials with limited electrical resistance as specified in G.4.3b; and provision of electrically conductive paths from ME EQUIPMENT or its parts to a conductive floor, protective earth or potential equalization system, or via wheels to an antistatic floor of medical room.

ME EQUIPMENT, its parts or components producing sparks in NORMAL USE and CONDITIONS must comply with temperature requirements of G.5.2, and Umax and Imax occurring in their circuits. Alternatively, equipment may comply with IEC 60079-0 requirements for pressurized enclosures (IEC 60079-2), sand-filled enclosures (IEC 60079-5), or oil immersed equipment (IEC 60079-6), together with the main standard excluding G.5.2 to G.5.5.

ENCLOSURE requirements for CATEGORY AP/APG: No openings on top covers except for openings for controls covered by control knobs; openings in side-covers must prevent penetration of a solid cylindrical test rod of 4mm diameter applied in all possible directions without appreciable force; openings in base plates must prevent penetration of a solid cylindrical test rod of 12mm diameter applied in all directions without appreciable force.
